about: The 700 lakes as drawn. LakeMap.png gives every pixel its lake's id (red + 256 x green; 0 where there is no lake). The lakes' shores are in no file as lines: they are the edges of LakeMap.png's patches.
order: Largest first: id 1 is the largest lake.

fields.px, km2: its size: pixels of LakeMap.png, and those times 0.112225
fields.middle: [x, y], the average of its pixels, which for a crooked lake may lie outside it
fields.point_inside: [x, y], a pixel that is in the lake: the one furthest from its shore
fields.box: [x0, y0, x1, y1], the smallest box that holds it
fields.kingdoms: how many of its pixels lie in each kingdom of KingdomMap.png (a border may run through a lake)
fields.kind: what made it when the water was worked out: caldera, crater, salt, or where on a stream it lies (trunk: on a main river; stream; head: at a valley's head; foot: where a river leaves the mountains; high: a mountain tarn; low; any)
fields.surface_m: the height of its surface above the sea. Elevation.png holds its bed, which is lower
fields.has_outlet: false for the salt lake, which two rivers end in, and for the six crater lakes, which no stream enters or leaves
fields.outlet: [x, y], the middle of the half-size cell where its water leaves it (Drainage.json)
fields.drainage_lakes: the ids, in DrainageLakes.png and Drainage.json, of the lakes of the drainage that it is drawn from, the largest first
